head: re-run mhw mcp render
why: The opening line of the managed block in the Codex config.toml tells the reader how to regenerate it. The original named global/mcp/mcp_render.py, which this slice deletes; the Node renderer names the command that replaces it, mhw mcp render. The block's servers, its stamp and every other byte are still compared. Consequence on an installed machine: an existing block keeps the old line, so mhw mcp render --check reports the Codex config as DRIFT (no server change) until the owner runs mhw mcp render once; install.sh does not run that mode, so no install changes it.

head: not valid TOML \([^\n]*\); left untouched
replace: not valid TOML (<the parser's message>); left untouched
why: A config.toml that does not parse is refused with the parser's own message in brackets: tomllib's in the original ("Invalid value (at line 1, column 9)"), smol-toml's in the Node renderer, which parses the same TOML 1.0 with the S10 guard (src/render/toml-guard.js). The refusal, its exit code (3) and the untouched file are still compared; only the bracketed text differs.

head: usage: mhw mcp render
why: The usage lines of the policy and active-set modes name the program: mcp_render.py in the original, mhw mcp render in the Node renderer. The rest of each line, the stream and the exit code (2) are still compared.

head: \(mhw mcp render --policy, ADR-0038\)
why: The POLICY line, which says a policy server is rendered on that surface by the policy mode, names that mode's command: mcp_render.py --policy in the original, mhw mcp render --policy in the Node renderer. The surface, the server names and the rest of the line are still compared.

head: (render them with|copy runs and) mhw mcp render
why: Two active-set report lines name the renderer: an ABSENT line ("render them with ...") and the REPORT line for a policy conflict ("... and ... refuses the local copy"). global/mcp/mcp_active.py, which prints them, now names mhw mcp render, the command that replaces the deleted mcp_render.py; mhw status (global/workstation.py) shows those lines and its tests are updated with them. The rest of each line, the server names, counts and exit codes are still compared.
